uncited: This family extends NeRF architectures to quantify prediction confidence, addressing artifacts, redundancy, and geometry collapse in sparse or unstructured data.

It differs from standard NeRF by modeling outputs as distributions (Gaussian) rather than deterministic points, and from sibling uncertainty methods by specific integrations like conformal prediction or semantic consistency constraints.

The core task of a NeRF network architecture is to learn a continuous volumetric scene representation $F_\Theta: (\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d}) \rightarrow (\sigma, \mathbf{c})$, where $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ is the spatial position, $\mathbf{d} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ is the viewing direction, $\sigma$ is the volume density, and $\mathbf{c}$ is the view-dependent color.
The rendering process integrates these outputs along rays using standard volume rendering equations.
It was developed to handle segmentation errors and background leakage in dynamic scenes.
